routes.title: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: Smith theory and mod p functoriality
routes.brief: Plan Smith theory for the cohomology of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and the mod p functoriality it produces. The final theorems are the paper's Theorem 4.4 and Theorem 5.8 and its Theorem 6.5. Theorem 4.4: let G be locally compact totally disconnected, K a compact open subgroup, X a locally compact Hausdorff space with a free proper right K-action and a continuous right G-action, and let sigma of order p act compatibly on G, K and X, with X/K of finite cohomological dimension and K sigma-plain; then, regarding H^*(X/K) and H^*(X^sigma/K^sigma) as modules over H(G,K)^sigma by restriction and through the Brauer homomorphism, every composition factor of the second is a composition factor of the first, and, when both Hecke algebras are commutative integral domains, every Hecke eigenvalue chi of the second gives the eigenvalue chi o nBr of the first. Theorem 5.8 (the First Main Theorem): for G semisimple over a number field F with sigma of order p and H = G^sigma connected, sigma-stable level K with U = K^sigma, and V a nonempty set of sigma-good places, H(G_V,K_V) and H(H_V,U_V) are commutative integral domains and every Hecke eigensystem chi occurring in H^*([H]_U ; k) gives the eigensystem chi o nBr occurring in H^*([G]_K ; k), with no assumption that either class lifts to characteristic zero. Theorem 6.5: with the same data, V finite and S a finite set of finite places disjoint from V and from the places above p, every irreducible subquotient of the H_S-module pi(chi) is linked with an irreducible subquotient of the G_S-module Pi(chi o nBr), where linkage means that the Frobenius twist occurs in the Tate cohomology. Cover: Tate cohomology of an order p action on the compactly supported sections of an equivariant sheaf on an l-space, and on a commutative k-algebra, with the bijection Hom(A,k)^sigma = Hom(T^0 A,k) that makes characters extend uniquely; sigma-plain compact open subgroups and the nonabelian cohomology they are defined by; the Brauer homomorphism of Hecke algebras and its normalization nBr; the Smith double complex, the degeneration of one of its spectral sequences and the convergence of the other; the sigma-action set-up on a pair of locally symmetric spaces, sigma-good places and the fact that almost all places are sigma-good; the identification of [H]_U with a union of connected components of the sigma-fixed locus; linkage of local representations, the conjectures of section 6.3, and the behaviour at ramified places; and the definition of a sigma-dual homomorphism together with the restatement of Theorem 5.8 as a functorial lift of modular Galois representations. Import from: Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces) for the spaces, their local systems and chain complexes and the Hecke correspondences on them; Adelic algebraic groups and arithmetic quotients (AdelicAlgebraicGroups) for adelic points, level maps and reduction theory; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) for the smooth category over k, admissibility, Hecke algebras over rings and the Satake isomorphism; and Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: prime-order automorphisms, dual norms and sigma-dual homomorphisms in characteristic p (SigmaDualHomomorphismsInCharacteristicP) for the computation of nBr on Satake parameters and for the existence of sigma-dual homomorphisms. Tate cohomology of a finite group is already in the libraries and must not be rebuilt.
routes.reason: The parent roadmap owns exactly the objects this part of the paper acts on: the symmetric space and its arithmetic quotients (ALS.0), local systems and chain complexes at finite level (ALS.1), and Hecke correspondences on those complexes with their coherence data in the derived category (ALS.3). What the paper adds is a Z/p-action on that whole package and the fixed-point localisation it supports: Tate cohomology of the action on sheaves over l-spaces and on Hecke algebras, the Brauer homomorphism and its normalization, the Smith double complex, and the identification of [H]_U with a union of components of the sigma-fixed locus. None of that is planned anywhere in the atlas: a search for Smith theory returns nothing, and the only Tate cohomology in the atlas is the class-formation layer of the Tau Ceti class field theory roadmap. It is new layers in the direction of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces rather than a new roadmap, because every statement is about the cohomology of the spaces that roadmap builds and about the Hecke action it constructs. It is deliberately disjoint from the other Part II proposed for the same parent, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpacesPartII (the derived Hecke algebra and the reciprocity law, from PAPER-VENKATESH-19), which plans a derived enhancement of the Hecke action in characteristic zero and says nothing about group actions on the spaces.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: prime-order automorphisms, dual norms and σ-dual homomorphisms in characteristic p
routes.brief: Plan the structure theory in characteristic p that computes the Brauer homomorphism on Satake parameters and constructs sigma-dual homomorphisms of L-groups. The final theorems are the paper's Theorem of section 8.1 and its Theorem 9.1. Theorem of section 8.1: let H = G^sigma be connected with sigma of prime order p, let v be a sigma-good place with Frobenius element gamma, fix local pseudoroots for G and H, let N-hat : T-hat_H to T-hat_G be the dual norm attached to a gamma-admissible Borel class and L-hat_gamma the associated dual Levi; then for every k-point x of (H-hat semidirect gamma) quotient H-hat there is t in T-hat_H(k) such that t rho_H^{-1}(gamma) represents x and N-hat(t) rho_G^{-1}(gamma) represents the image of x under Spec(nBr), and t may be chosen so that N-hat(t) lies in the centre of L-hat_gamma. Theorem 9.1 (the Second Main Theorem): if G is simply connected, sigma is an F-rational automorphism of prime order and H = G^sigma is semisimple, and (Lie G, Lie H) contains no factor isomorphic to (e_6, sl_3^3 or sl_6 x sl_2 or sp_8), then a sigma-dual homomorphism ^Lpsi : ^LH to ^LG exists with respect to the canonical pseudoroots. Cover: the canonical torus of a reductive group and global and canonical pseudoroots; Borel-de Siebenthal subgroups for an inner automorphism of order p and the dual endoscopic subgroups of G-hat, with the quasi-closed sets of roots that classify them; the C-group and the c-group and the PGL_2 counterexample showing that no sigma-dual homomorphism of L-groups or of C-groups need exist; the centraliser theory of section 8, namely that the centraliser of a maximal torus of H is a maximal torus of G, the split part of a gamma-fixed torus, the Levi L_G(gamma) and its derived group, gamma-admissible Borels with their existence lemma, the norm and dual norm homomorphisms, the rationality statements and the extension of unramified characters to the parabolic; the criterion of section 8.15 for recognising a sigma-dual homomorphism and Lemma 8.16; and the whole construction of sections 9 to 12: cyclic base change, the passage to the simply connected cover, the reduction to the absolutely almost simple case, the classification tables, Borel triples and the extension of psi_1 to the dual groups, the inner case with the element U for p = 3, the criteria for inner involutions and for pinned automorphisms with the exceptional isogenies they use, and the remaining computations including the embedding of Sp(2n) into the pinned fixed points of SO(2n+2) in characteristic 2 and the order 5 inner automorphism of E_8 with fixed points sl_5 x sl_5. Import from: Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) for algebraic groups, tori, Borel and parabolic subgroups, root data with their Galois action, pinned Chevalley-Demazure group schemes, the Frobenius on points and the special isogenies in characteristics 2 and 3, which are existing work and must not be re-planned; Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for relative roots, hyperspecial parahorics and the integral dual group and L-group; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) for the Satake isomorphism and unramified parabolic induction; and Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: Smith theory and mod p functoriality (SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality) for the Brauer homomorphism, its normalization and the definition of a sigma-dual homomorphism.
routes.reason: Sections 8 to 12 are almost pure structure theory of reductive groups in characteristic p: fixed subgroups of an automorphism of prime order, Borel-de Siebenthal and its dual, centralisers of the split part of a gamma-fixed torus, admissible Borels and the parabolic they generate, norm and dual norm maps between tori and their duals, pinned automorphisms with their invariants e_alpha, f_alpha and theta_alpha, exceptional isogenies, and explicit Weyl group and root computations in E_7 and E_8. The Tau Ceti reductive-groups roadmap is the roadmap in that direction: it plans Borel and parabolic subgroups, root data with their Galois action, pinned Chevalley-Demazure group schemes over Z with their base change and Frobenius on points, and the special isogenies in characteristics 2 and 3. Because it is a Tau Ceti roadmap it is existing work and is never re-planned, so what extends it is a Part II (PROTOCOL section 15). Nothing in it, nor in ReductiveGroupsPartII, plans Borel-de Siebenthal, the endoscopic subgroups of the dual group, admissible Borel classes, dual norms, the C-group and c-group, or the existence of sigma-dual homomorphisms, and no other roadmap goes in that direction. The Theorem of section 8.1 is placed here with the rest of section 8 because its content is the dual norm attached to an admissible Borel class; it imports the Brauer homomorphism itself from the Part II of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces proposed above.

Section 7 is, in the authors' own description, folklore on the Satake transform written out because they know no reference with characteristic p coefficients, and it lands inside layers this roadmap already plans. SR.4 plans the Satake transform for unramified G at a hyperspecial K, the isomorphism with the appropriate invariant algebra on the dual torus retaining the relative Weyl group and Frobenius action, with the coefficients and the q-half normalization to be specified and the unnormalized integral form recorded separately, and the identification of Hecke eigencharacters with unramified semisimple parameters. That is exactly what sections 7.1 to 7.4 and 7.6 supply over k: the twisted action w * a = wa sqrt(Sigma^*_G / w Sigma^*_G)(q_v) of the restricted Weyl group, which removes the need to choose a square root of q_v; the invariant theory lemma identifying W_0-invariant functions on the dual torus with G-hat-invariant functions on G-hat semidirect Frob_v; local pseudoroots as the canonical substitute for the q-half normalization; the Satake parameter of an unnormalized parabolic induction; and Theorem 7.9, which states the isomorphism canonically in terms of the c-group. The correspondence between unramified k^*-valued characters of a torus and elements of T-hat(k) is the base case of the same identification. SR.1 plans Hecke algebras over rings and says explicitly that characteristic p is to be treated in the smooth action category with integral double-coset operators, which is where Fun_G(S x S) belongs; SR.0 plans the smooth category and admissibility over arbitrary coefficients; and SR.2 plans unnormalized induction from a parabolic. This roadmap is a campaign roadmap, not a Tau Ceti one, so it may take the paper as a source.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:1407.2346v1 (9 July 2014), §12.2, the second unnumbered Proposition after Proposition 12.3, part (2)
sourceIssues.printed: $\LL_G(U^2)$ is the Levi obtained by adjoining the roots to $\TT$ the roots ±x_1, ±y_3, ±y_1, ±y_3
sourceIssues.correction: The four root pairs are ±x_1, ±x_3, ±y_1, ±y_3: the second entry should be ±x_3, not a second ±y_3.
sourceIssues.reason: As printed the list names only three distinct root pairs, which cannot give the derived group SL_2^4 asserted two lines later. Computing directly in the E_8 root system with the simple roots of (12.1) and the roots x_1, x_2, x_3, y_1, y_2, y_3 of (12.3): U is orthogonal, has order 4 and equals s_{x_1}s_{x_2+x_3}s_{-x_1-x_2}s_{y_1}s_{y_2+y_3}s_{-y_1-y_2} exactly, L_G(U) has 24 roots, and the centraliser of the identity component of T^{U^2}, that is the set of roots orthogonal to the fixed space of U^2, consists of exactly eight roots, namely ±x_1, ±x_3, ±y_1, ±y_3. These four are orthogonal and satisfy U^2 v = -v, so they span the (-1)-eigenspace of U^2 and give SL_2^4. The deleted proof in the source file makes the same statement: 'x_1, x_3, y_1, y_3 are orthogonal and generate the (-1)-eigenspace of U^2'.
